data.why: The repository ships complete demo corpora (24 synthetic interviews with reference codings in analyses/, 80 congressional-hearing transcripts, and 4 coding frameworks) that already exercise every tab without a model or key, so no synthetic data needs to be written.

goals: Approve a literature-grounded coding framework dimension by dimension before coding any transcript
Confirm, revise or delete model-proposed codes on a transcript and build a full audit trail of interpretive decisions
Build a reliability sampling frame from respondent turns and compute Cohen's kappa, PABAK, Gwet's AC1 and Krippendorff's alpha with a disagreement list
Run cross-tabulations and co-occurrence analyses of codes against respondent descriptors, respecting chi-square assumption checks
Turn a coder's completed reliability sheet into analysable records and run theme induction or model-free theme grouping on the coded corpus
Export the coded corpus as annotated Word documents, Excel tables and a Gioia-style data structure figure

review.summary: The tree is accurate and well-evidenced for everything that runs without a model. The reliability, review, cross-analysis and theme phases nest sensibly, and the screens match the labels. But it leaves out the README's two headline stages, building the framework from the literature and actually coding transcripts, and it presents a coder-vs-AI reliability report as if it compared two coders, so it needs those additions and corrections before filing.
